subject.title: fix(shared): bound ignore-file reads during workspace scans

question: Should an oversized ignore file at the fixed 4 MiB cap terminally hide its directory subtree, or should the scanner fail visibly with an actionable diagnostic instead?
rationale: Both paths avoid unbounded memory use, but they differ materially for existing workspaces: terminal exclusion can silently remove skills and files from discovery, while a visible failure changes scan availability and operator workflow.

options.title: Use a visible scan failure
options.body: Keep the bounded read but surface an actionable oversized-ignore diagnostic instead of silently omitting the subtree.

options.title: Approve terminal subtree exclusion
options.body: Accept the 4 MiB cap and fail-closed discovery behavior as the compatibility contract, with clear documentation and exact-head proof.

recommendation.title: Use a visible scan failure
recommendation.body: Keep the bounded read but surface an actionable oversized-ignore diagnostic instead of silently omitting the subtree.
